newsitem.title: CHINA: China stocks plunge on quota, rebound expected.
newsitem.headline: China stocks plunge on quota, rebound expected.

text.p: China's stock prices plunged in early trade on Friday after Beijing announced a huge quota for stock issues in 1997 but good market fundamentals will trim losses during the day, brokers said.
A few minutes after the opening, Shanghai's A share index was down 51.157 points or 3.45 percent to 1,432.086 points and the B share index had shed 2.199 points or 2.48 percent to 86.571 points.
In Shenzhen, the A index lost 17.73 points or 3.44 percent to 497.74 points and the B index shed 3.79 points or 2.20 percent to 168.73 points.

The Securities Commission under the State Council (cabinet) and the State Planning Commission on Thursday announced a quota for new stock issues in 1997 of 30 billion yuan, a huge increase over the 1996 quota of 15 billion.

Brokers said the market had been unprepared for such a huge quota and had not expected Beijing to announce this year's quota so soon. China usually announces each year's share listing quota at the end of the year.
"Investors were caught completely unprepared for such an announcement," said one trader. "Panic selling emerged in the first few minutes of trading."

But brokers said market fundamentals were still good with the improvement of China's economy and performance of listed firms and that the indices were likely to trim losses for the rest of the session on Friday.

"The indices will recover to some extent for the rest of the session today with good market fundamentals changing little," said a broker. "The indices are likely to move in negative territory for the day but the loss margin might be trimmed to around two percent."
